findings.title: Negative offset slicing on a Django queryset raises an error; the gate is also user-controllable
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative `cursor.offset` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features` is true. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment claiming 'the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is wrong. The offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative ints). So an admin (or superuser) who sends `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative-offset cursor gets a 500. Any case where it does not error (for example a mixed slice) would bypass the intended pagination bounds, so the claim that this gives 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' is a data-exposure risk.

findings.title: Change to the shared BasePaginator lets negative offsets reach the ORM for all prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` now passes an unclamped, user-controlled negative offset to `queryset[...]` whenever `is_prev` is set. This affects every BasePaginator subclass across Sentry, not only the new opt-in path. Previously the offset was passed through as-is, so negative values already failed. The change adds no protection, and the comment ('safe because the queryset handles boundary conditions') is false. A crafted prev cursor such as `0:-5:1` triggers an AssertionError (500) on any paginated endpoint. The stop computation is also inconsistent: `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` can be smaller than the start.

findings.title: Authorization gate for the experimental paginator is weak and can crash
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for superusers who are not org members, which raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, so a non-member non-superuser would hit it, and the check is hard to reason about overall. The feature is also exposed through a plain query parameter. Combined with the negative offset handling, this opens an unsafe code path to a broad set of org members (anyone with global access). Trailing whitespace also appears on lines 71 and 89.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is wrong for datetime ordering and duplicates BasePaginator logic
findings.body: The endpoint uses `order_by="-datetime"` with OptimizedCursorPaginator, whose `get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime'))`. `floor` on a datetime raises TypeError. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw value instead of converting it back to a datetime, as DateTimePaginator does. So the optimized path fails on the first request that returns results. Beyond that, the class copies about 70 lines of BasePaginator.get_result, which invites drift. It also has no tests.

findings.title: Misleading comment claims negative offsets are supported
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for efficient reverse pagination. The code is unchanged (`int(offset)`) and nothing validates or supports negative values downstream. The comment documents unsupported, unsafe behavior and will mislead maintainers.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses the raw offset after negative-offset slicing
findings.body: `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses `offset`, which may be negative, while the slice used `start_offset`. The condition is meaningless for negative offsets, so an extra row is not trimmed and prev pages return wrong or duplicated rows.
